question.text:
Consider the following sequence:

\[ 2, \quad 0, \quad -2, \quad -4, \quad -6, \quad \dots \] The recursive formula for this sequence is given by \[ a_{n+1} = a_{n} + \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,, \qquad a_1 = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,. \] From left to right, what are the missing values?
question.explanation:
Notice that the first term of the sequence is $a_1 = {\color{blue}2}.$

Inspecting the terms of the sequence, we see that we always get the next term by subtracting $2.$ This is the same as adding ${\color{red}-2}.$

Therefore, the recursive rule must be the following:

\[ a_{n+1} = a_{n} + \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{({\color{red}-2})}\,, \qquad a_1 = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{{\color{blue}2}} \]

So, the missing values are $-2$ and $2.$

example.title: Writing a Recursive Formula for a Sequence

question.text: Consider the following sequence: \[ -1, \quad \dfrac{1}{2}, \quad -\dfrac{1}{4}, \quad \dfrac{1}{8}, \quad -\dfrac{1}{16}, \quad \dots \] The recursive formula for this sequence is given by \[ a_{n+1} = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\cdot a_n, \qquad a_1 = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,. \] From left to right, what are the missing values?
question.explanation:
Notice that the first term of the sequence is $a_1 = {\color{blue}-1}.$

Inspecting the terms of the sequence, we see that we always get the next term by dividing by $-2.$ This is the same as multiplying by ${\color{red}-\dfrac{1}{2}}.$

Therefore, the recursive rule must be the following: \[ a_{n+1} = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\color{red}-\dfrac{1}{2}} \cdot a_n, \qquad a_1 = \bbox[3pt, border: 1pt solid black]{\color{blue}-1} \]

So, the missing values are $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $-1.$

example.title: Writing a Recursive Formula for a Sequence

question.explanation:
The recursive formula is \[ a_{n+1}=7a_n - 3. \] where $a_1={\color{blue}1}.$

We use this formula to compute the terms $a_2$ and $a_3$ as follows:

  • We first compute $a_2$ by substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula: \begin{align*} a_{n+1} &= 7a_n - 3 \\[5pt] a_{1+1} & =7a_1 - 3 \\[5pt] a_{2} & =7a_1 - 3 \\[5pt] a_2 & = 7({\color{blue}1})- 3 \\[5pt] a_2 & = {\color{red}4} \end{align*}

  • Then, we compute $a_3$ by substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula: \begin{align*} a_{n+1} &= 7a_n - 3 \\[5pt] a_{2+1} & = 7a_2 - 3 \\[5pt] a_{3} & = 7a_2 - 3 \\[5pt] a_3 & = 7({\color{red}4}) - 3 \\[5pt] a_3 & = 25 \end{align*}

Therefore, $a_3=25.$
